title: Eyes and vision (chapter in Scorpion Biology and Research)
why: Gives the optics of scorpion median and lateral eyes, which would replace the invented sharpness and zones of the scorpion view.

title: Understanding the cephalic eyes of pulmonate gastropods: a review
why: Its tables of eye size, optics and sampling for many land and freshwater snails would set the snail view's sharpness beyond the single red slug figure; it is openly licensed on the Biodiversity Heritage Library, which refused automated reading.

title: The visual system of Myriapoda
journal: Springer Series in Vision Research (book chapter)
why: A survey of millipede and centipede eyes that may give fields and facet angles, replacing the inferred centipede sharpness and testing the millipede value.

authors: Müller CHG, Rosenberg J, Richter S, Meyer-Rochow VB
title: The compound eye of Scutigera coleoptrata (Linnaeus, 1758) (Chilopoda: Notostigmophora): an ultrastructural reinvestigation that adds support to the Mandibulata concept
why: Ommatidial geometry of the house centipede, the most recorded centipede, would replace the invented 0.05 cycles per degree.

title: The lateral eyes of the scorpion, Androctonus australis
why: Lateral eye structure would settle whether the side zones of the scorpion view should carry any image at all.

title: The absolute sensitivity of the median and lateral eyes of the scorpion, Androctonus australis L. (Buthidae, Scorpiones)
why: Settles whether the lateral eyes exceed the median eyes by 1 log unit or by 10, which sets the night gain of the side zones.

title: Neurobiology of a circadian clock in the visual system of scorpions. In: Barth FG (ed.) Neurobiology of Arachnids, pp. 351-376
why: The scorpion chapter missing from the owner's partial copy of Barth (1985); it would give the night-state sensitivity and the eye physiology behind the scorpion view.

title: Fan worm eyes
why: Radiolar eye arrangements and their resolution would set the shadow-alarm threshold for fan worms in the worm view.

authors: Gaffin DD, Bumm LA, Taylor MS, Popokina NV, Mann SN
title: Scorpion fluorescence and reaction to light
journal: Animal Behaviour (OpenAlex dates it 2011; the Zenodo record gives 1 February 2012)
why: Gives the wavelengths and intensities behind the cuticle-as-light-collector result, which the glowing-rim effect would follow; Zenodo record 895450 holds a copy whose file was refused here.

title: Light wavelength biases of scorpions
why: Behavioural weighting of wavelengths would correct the scorpion colour matrix.

title: Scorpion lateral eyes: extremely sensitive receptors of Zeitgeber stimuli
why: Confirms the lateral eyes' role and sensitivity behind the side zones.

title: Behavioural responses to visual stimuli by the snail Littorina irrorata
why: Settles whether the 14.5 degrees attributed to the garden snail belongs to this periwinkle.

authors: Hamilton PV, Ardizzoni SC, Penn JS
title: Eye structure and optics in the intertidal snail, Littorina irrorata
why: Periwinkle optics for a later conch and periwinkle split of the snail view.

title: The spectral sensitivity of the dark-adapted eye of Helix pomatia L.
why: Confirms the single blue-green pigment in the Roman snail itself, behind the snail colour row.

title: A millipede compound eye mediating low-resolution vision
why: The full text (openly licensed, unreachable here) gives the facet count and field of the julid eye behind the millipede view.

authors: Willemart RH, Farine J-P, Gnaspini P
title: Sensory biology of Phalangida harvestmen (Arachnida, Opiliones): a review, with new morphological data on 18 species
why: The review's evidence on harvestman eyes and phototaxis would test the harvestman picture's two side windows and coarse sight.

title: Structure and function of the eyes of two species of opilionid from New Zealand glow-worm caves (Megalopsalis tumida: Palpatores, and Hendea myersi cavernicola: Laniatores)
journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
why: Spectral peaks in nanometres and visual fields for harvestman eyes.

title: The distribution and morphology of probable photoreceptors in eight species of ticks (Ixodoidea)
why: Eyes and light-sensitive cells across tick genera, testing the eyed and eyeless rows.

authors: Mitchell RD, Zhu J, Carr AL, Dhammi A, Cave GL, Sonenshine DE, Roe RM
title: Infrared light detection by the Haller's organ of adult American dog ticks, Dermacentor variabilis (Ixodida: Ixodidae)
why: Wavelengths of the heat sense in the most recorded tick, behind the Heat row.

title: Sensory responses and related behaviour (chapter)
why: The full chapter on centipede light, touch and smell responses behind several centipede rows.

title: On the responses to environmental stimuli, and the sensory physiology of millipedes (Diplopoda)
journal: Proceedings of the Zoological Society of London
why: The full paper on the greenhouse millipede's senses behind most millipede rows.

title: Orientation to vibrations in sand by the nocturnal scorpion Paruroctonus mesaensis: mechanism of target localization
why: Timing cues behind the ripples-in-sand effect.
